title: Race Conditions and Deadlocks knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best demonstrates understanding of “Race Conditions and Deadlocks”?
options: Replace all built-in features with a third-party framework regardless of the task.
Skip tests because a short example ran once.
Use Race Conditions and Deadlocks deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
Assume Ruby automatically guarantees every business rule and external system behavior.
questions.answer_key: Use Race Conditions and Deadlocks deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case.
questions.explanation: Use Race Conditions and Deadlocks deliberately: state the expected behavior, apply it in a small example, and verify a boundary case. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: When applying “Race Conditions and Deadlocks”, which practice is the most reliable?
options: Treat all Ruby versions and third-party dependencies as identical.
Keep the race conditions and deadlocks rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
Silence all errors and trust the result without inspecting inputs.
Use unrelated global state so every part of the program can modify the same value.
questions.answer_key: Keep the race conditions and deadlocks rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Keep the race conditions and deadlocks rule explicit, then test the result against the relevant input and runtime assumptions. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.

questions.prompt: If a result involving “Race Conditions and Deadlocks” differs from your prediction, what should you do first?
options: When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code.
Catch every exception and continue even if the program state is unknown.
Disable validation or security checks to make the example pass faster.
Change several unrelated lines at once and avoid reproducing the problem.
questions.answer_key: When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code.
questions.explanation: When behavior differs from your prediction, reproduce the smallest case, inspect the diagnostic, and check the supported documentation before changing code. The alternatives overstate Ruby guarantees or encourage unverified behavior.
